name: rust-libbin-test-coverage
body:
source: the `libbin-fix` brief's test-coverage finding, extended by review `libbin-fix/feedback-2` and corrected by the coordinator's scan-scope finding. Gap: no test exercises either end of the module-prefix fix. The only Rust test fixture (`testdata/rust/fixture`) is lib-only and the only bin fixture in the tests is the frontend's own bin-only package, so neither the new collision nor the stability of the currently-scanning multi-target case is guarded.

Correction (why not `testdata/`): `testdata/**` is inside apg's own scan scope — `testdata/rust/fixture/src/lib.rs`, `.../src/shapes.rs` and `.../tests/it.rs` are File nodes in this branch's graph, i.e. the repo's own `apg scan` scans them. That scan is run by the installed (pre-fix) binary, so a committed default lib+bin fixture would make the next repo scan render two crate roots at one FQN and panic — the parent-cannot-depend-on-the-child trap one level down: the change-set would break the very scan it is verified against. The fixtures are therefore generated at test time in scratch directories under `std::env::temp_dir()`, never committed under `testdata/`. This matches the existing e2e pattern: `rust.apg.tests.rust_frontend_records` (`src/main.rs:3148–3172`, `rust_frontend_records(repo_dir: &Path)`) already runs the staged rust frontend over an arbitrary directory and feeds its records to the in-process ingestor, and the repo's self-contained-e2e rule (documented as `global.constraint.self-contained-tests`) requires every e2e scenario to build its own scratch tree.

Resolution (for the plan): two scratch packages, each written at test time under `std::env::temp_dir()` and driven by an e2e test through the staged rust frontend's scanner spool + the in-process ingestor (the `rust_frontend_records` pattern):

1. Collision case — a scratch default lib+bin package, `[package] name = "foo"` with `src/lib.rs` (lib target `foo`) and `src/main.rs` (bin target `foo`), no explicit `[lib]`/`[[bin]]`. Assertion: the frontend + ingestor completes without a duplicate-FQN panic, and the two crate roots render distinct module FQNs — each crate's units enumerate under its own prefix.

2. Stability case — a scratch multi-target package with distinct target names, `[package] name = "foo"`, `[lib] name = "foo"`, `[[bin]] name = "foo-cli"`. This package scans today (distinct display names fall back to distinct prefixes `rust.foo` and `rust.foo-cli`). Assertion (regression): after the fix it renders exactly the current module FQNs — `rust.foo` and `rust.foo-cli` — with no unit FQN renamed; pin the two FQN literals in the test so any drift fails loudly. This is the `requirements.constraint.rust-crate-fqn-stability` guarantee for a currently-scanning package.

No committed fixture under `testdata/` is added by this change-set, so the plan declares no `testdata/**` planned nodes. [autonomous]
